brief: A color palette generator that works like a musical instrument — play colors, harmonies lock like chords

dominant_strengths: Clean monospace labels and consistent uppercase tracking give the control panel a tidy, instrument-like operator feel
Restrained dark chrome lets color swatches dominate as the primary expressive surface, aligning with the play-colors metaphor
Sensible information architecture: modes, octave, root note read as a coherent musical control stack
dominant_weaknesses: Only two giant color blocks render despite 12 chromatic note labels — the keyboard metaphor is promised in the header but not built
Red and orange swatches clash and look arbitrary rather than harmonically derived, undermining the entire 'chords lock' premise
Empty 'Current Harmony' panel and missing playback affordances make the musical interaction feel inert and unfinished
fix_priorities: Render all 12 chromatic note columns as playable keys with hover/active states to deliver the instrument metaphor
Generate swatches algorithmically from a harmonic color theory model so Major/Minor/Dorian visibly produce different palettes
Populate Current Harmony with locked chord swatches, hex values, and a play/sequence control
Tighten the color system — coordinated hues with shared saturation/lightness — so chords feel consonant, not random
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral is muted by clashing reds, behavioral is broken by absent keys and feedback, and reflective payoff never arrives because the harmony panel is empty.
rationale.intent_fit: The scaffolding gestures at the brief but the core instrument — playable notes producing locked harmonic palettes — is not actually implemented on screen.
